abstract_sentences.text: Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) are capable of retrieving high-performing policy for any reward function specified directly at test-time, commonly referred to as zero-shot reinforcement learning (RL).

evidence.anchor: reward function specified directly at test-time

abstract_sentences.text: While this is a very efficient process in terms of compute, it can be less so in terms of data: as a standard assumption, BFMs require computing rewards over a non-negligible inference dataset, assuming either access to a functional form of rewards, or significant labeling efforts.

evidence.anchor: require computing rewards over a non-negligible inference dataset

abstract_sentences.text: To alleviate these limitations, we tackle the problem of task inference purely through interaction with the environment at test-time.

evidence.anchor: purely through interaction with the environment

abstract_sentences.text: We propose OpTI-BFM, an optimistic decision criterion that directly models uncertainty over reward functions and guides BFMs in data collection for task inference.

evidence.anchor: models uncertainty over reward functions

abstract_sentences.text: Formally, we provide a regret bound for well-trained BFMs through a direct connection to upper-confidence algorithms for linear bandits.

evidence.anchor: regret bound for well-trained BFMs

abstract_sentences.text: Empirically, we evaluate OpTI-BFM on established zero-shot benchmarks, and observe that it enables successor-features-based BFMs to identify and optimize an unseen reward function in a handful of episodes with minimal compute overhead.

evidence.anchor: identify and optimize an unseen reward function

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 1 (informal)

evidence.anchor: it incurs an expected regret of O-tilde (d sqrt n)

equation_theory_inventory.description: Under A1–A4 and episode-start updates, expected regret is O-tilde(d sqrt(n)); formalized as Proposition 5.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 2

evidence.anchor: in Loewner order

equation_theory_inventory.description: The empirical return-level SF outer product is bounded by c_H times the within-episode feature matrix.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 3

evidence.anchor: V_n grows at least as fast as W_n

equation_theory_inventory.description: Reward-level precision V_n is at least W_n/c_H in Loewner order.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 4

evidence.anchor: confidence ellipsoids at least as tight

equation_theory_inventory.description: The V_n inverse norm is at most sqrt(c_H) times the W_n inverse norm.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 1

evidence.anchor: true parameter z_r is contained in confidence sets

equation_theory_inventory.description: A uniform-in-time self-normalized confidence radius contains z_r with probability at least 1-delta.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 5 (formal)

evidence.anchor: incurs an expected regret of O-tilde(d sqrt n)

equation_theory_inventory.description: Under A1–A4 and episode-start exact UCB, OpTI-BFM has expected regret O-tilde(d sqrt(n)).

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proposition 6

evidence.anchor: useful properties that are used in the proofs above

equation_theory_inventory.description: A determinant upper bound follows from bounded feature norms and AM-GM.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 1

evidence.anchor: commonly referred to as the elliptical potential lemma

equation_theory_inventory.description: Elliptical potential sum is bounded by twice the log determinant ratio.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Proposition 2

evidence.anchor: direct application of a Cauchy-Schwarz inequality

equation_theory_inventory.description: Cauchy–Schwarz proves the Loewner outer-product inequality.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Proposition 3

evidence.anchor: Summing over episodes on both sides

equation_theory_inventory.description: Summing the Proposition 2 matrix inequality and adding lambda I proves the precision order.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Proposition 4

evidence.anchor: As the inverse thus reverses order

equation_theory_inventory.description: Matrix inverse order and quadratic-form comparison prove the norm relation.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Proposition 5

evidence.anchor: We will proceed as in the standard regret bound

equation_theory_inventory.description: The proof conditions on the confidence event, bounds instantaneous regret, and applies the elliptical potential lemma.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Proposition 6

evidence.anchor: using the AM-GM inequality

equation_theory_inventory.description: AM-GM and trace bounds establish the determinant inequality.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 1

evidence.anchor: Telescoping the previous result

equation_theory_inventory.description: Determinant lemma telescoping establishes the elliptical-potential inequality.

final_judgment.single_storyline: OpTI-BFM converts low-dimensional BFM task embeddings into an online feature–reward regression problem; a confidence ellipsoid and optimistic acquisition choose informative behaviors while controlling regret, with the formal guarantee restricted to episode-level switching and idealized USF/linearity assumptions.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps SF/BFM notation, Eqs.7–12, Algorithm 1, A1–A4, the informal regret statement, main DMC comparison, active-data diagnostic, update-frequency test and variant questions.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, determinant/elliptical-potential details, compute timing, label-query curves, optimizer comparison, OGBench, misspecification/noise tests, per-task plots, FB losses/architecture, protocol and hyperparameters move to Appendix A–F; this makes timing, heterogeneity and reproduction conditions less self-sufficient.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 sets an offline-versus-online contrast, Eqs.7–12 form a contiguous estimator→uncertainty→optimism chain, and Sections 5.1–5.5 each answer a named evaluation question with appendix expansions.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The strongest practical per-step version lacks the theorem proved for episode-level updates; “minimal compute overhead” is qualitative in the abstract despite 4.6×/3.6× per-step latency, and pixel deployment remains untested.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: When a sequential agent has a low-dimensional latent and online feedback, align estimator, uncertainty object, acquisition rule, execution algorithm and boundary-matched ablations as one explicit evidence chain.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule assumes feedback is observable, the behavior family is already trained, latent–reward structure is approximately linear and data collection can be controlled; it does not directly transfer to unstructured high-dimensional latents or no-label deployment.
